content:
Maya R: customer hit a 422 on our rerank endpoint, they're sending a nested payload and the scores all come back identical. reported error: '422 Unprocessable Entity - Invalid input: unexpected object in "documents"'. they insist docs are 'documents with candidates inside' from another vendor. can we clarify what we accept and a short repro?

Anita C: can you paste the request they sent? also any request_id/trace id from our logs would help.

Maya R: paste below (sensitive fields redacted):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "best hotels in seattle",
    "documents": [
      {
        "doc_id": "d1",
        "passages": [
          {"text": "Hotel A description..."},
          {"text": "Hotel A review snippet..."}
        ],
        "candidates": [
          "Hotel A",
          "Hotel B",
          "Hotel C"
        ]
      },
      {
        "doc_id": "d2",
        "passages": [{"text":"Hotel B main blurb"}],
        "candidates": ["Hotel B","Hotel A"]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

Response:
```json
{"error":"422 Unprocessable Entity","message":"Invalid input: unexpected object in \"documents\""}
```

They also said that when they attempted a slightly different shape (documents as strings and a top-level candidates array) they got back scores that were all identical (0.5) across candidates, which looks like the reranker degenerated.

Jared L: quick clarification: our public schema expects either a flat list of candidate strings with a single query, or a top-level list of paired queries+candidate arrays. We do not accept nested candidate lists inside per-document objects. docs vs candidates vs passages got confused across vendor schemas. Example accepted shapes: 

1) Single-query, candidates flat:
```json
{
  "query": "best hotels in seattle",
  "candidates": ["Hotel A","Hotel B","Hotel C"]
}
```

2) Batch of queries each with own candidates (note: top-level array of objects, not "documents"):
```json
[
  {"query":"q1","candidates":["a","b"]},
  {"query":"q2","candidates":["x","y"]}
]
```

We deliberately reserved the key "documents" for a different endpoint (semantic-search) that accepts documents/passages for indexing/search. reusing "documents" here causes our v1/rerank parser to treat it as invalid.

Kevin P: regarding identical scores — that's often because our scorer sees empty or whitespace-only candidate text after our normalization step, or when candidates are nested we fall back to a degenerate branch that returns uniform logits. can you confirm whether the customers' nested "candidates" items are strings or objects? also how many candidates per query? we have a softmax numeric stability issue if >512 candidates in a single batch slice (we try to chunk, but some older runtime builds had a bug).

Maya R: in their bad payload candidates are strings, but nested under each document object. counts: most requests were ~40-80 candidates per query. they said updating to 10 candidates reduced identical scoring. request id from our logs: rq_01HkLk... (timestamp 2025-08-14T15:22:11Z).

deploy-bot: [automated] 2025-08-14T15:22:12Z - POST /v1/rerank rq_01HkLk... returned 422 from parser (schema mismatch).

Anita C: repro plan: 1) try their exact nested payload against staging; 2) try flattening to accepted shapes; 3) test >50 candidates to reproduce uniform scores; 4) collect runtimes and model logits. I'll run (1) and (2) now.

Anita C (later): confirmed on staging: nested "documents" payload -> 422 with same message. flattening payload to top-level candidates works and returns sensible varied scores. when I replicated >60 candidates in a single call I saw score collapse to near-uniform in the older runtime image (runtime:v2.4.1). upgraded runtime to v2.5.0 in staging fixed softmax instability for large batches.

Kevin P: thanks. action items:
- CS: send customer a short note explaining schema mismatch and give two example payloads (flat candidates or per-query array). include a sample quick-fix curl they can try.
- CS/Support: ask them to limit candidates to <=32 while we verify their upgrade path.
- Eng (Runtime): create a validation error with a clearer message when "documents" is supplied to /v1/rerank (rather than a generic 422). file ticket: RUNTIME-9983.
- Docs: add explicit examples for "documents" vs "candidates" and call out that "documents" is for search/index endpoints.

Jared L: quick suggested reply snippet for CS: 

"Thanks — it looks like your payload uses a nested 'documents' structure. Our rerank endpoint expects either a single query with a top-level 'candidates' array or a top-level array of {query,candidates} objects. Try this minimal fix: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "query": "best hotels in seattle",
    "candidates": ["Hotel A","Hotel B","Hotel C"]
  }'
```

If you need to score candidates grouped by document, please first flatten passages into candidate strings or call our search/index endpoint that accepts 'documents' with passages and then call rerank on the returned candidates."

Kevin P: I'll follow up on RUNTIME-9983 and push a better parser error message in the next patch. also adding a regression test for >64 candidates per call.

Maya R: sending the customer the note now, including the temporary candidate limit. closing this thread after eng ticket created. tagging QA to add a test. :white_check_mark:
notes: resolved: temporary mitigation documented; eng ticket RUNTIME-9983; docs update requested; customer advised to flatten payload or reduce candidates
